heading: Induction heads can form through several ordered stages
definition: formation is a sequence of separate sub-steps or several overlapping transitions, rather than one phase change.
summary: Several studies report successive steps in induction-head formation, including in a 3M attention-only language model and Pythia/OLMo training checkpoints. The observations do not always distinguish separate transitions, and evidence that heads in larger models begin participating at different times comes from one training run per model.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy/synthetic (usually size 'not stated' in counts): R2 for ordered stages. <1B: R2 for ordered sub-steps, including the 3M attention-only LM (arXiv:2402.02364#R1, arXiv:2402.02364#R5, arXiv:2402.02364#R7) and Pythia/OLMo checkpoints (arXiv:2609.19000#R1, arXiv:2609.19000#R2, arXiv:2609.19000#R3). Pythia-410m/160m shows previous-token-first ordering within a coarse window; separate formation transitions remain undetermined, rather than contradicted (arXiv:2607.06621#r18, arXiv:2607.06621#r19). 1-10B: R0 for staggered recruitment in Pythia 1B, OLMo 1B and OLMoE, with one training run per model (arXiv:2606.02378#r18, arXiv:2606.02378#r19, arXiv:2606.02378#r20). 10-100B and >100B: no coverage recorded in counts: versions.V7.studies_by_size.
suggested_status.reason: Retain R2 as the working suggestion for ordered stages. The 3M attention-only LM shows K-composition, previous-token behaviour and prefix matching developing in successive stages (arXiv:2402.02364#R1, arXiv:2402.02364#R5, arXiv:2402.02364#R7). Public Pythia/OLMo checkpoints show previous-token behaviour before induction or copying (arXiv:2609.19000#R1, arXiv:2609.19000#R2, arXiv:2609.19000#R3). In Pythia-410m/160m, previous-token behaviour rises first, followed by induction behaviour, the ICL proxy and wiring within 1–4B tokens. These observations neither establish nor exclude separate formation transitions; the explicit unresolved ordering concerns spectral structure versus function. This is not a limits_scope result for V7 (arXiv:2607.06621#r18, arXiv:2607.06621#r19). The supplied, unrecomputed counts report versions.V7.studies_tested = 21, versions.V7.verdicts.supports.studies = 17, versions.V7.verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 6 and versions.V7.verdicts.challenges.studies = 1; those totals precede the checker correction and must not be read as corrected verdict totals. V7 has no linked original (counts: versions.V7.original_sources_linked = []), and author independence among supporting studies is not recorded in the synthesis.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would finer-resolution Pythia checkpoints establish distinct formation transitions or coordinated changes within the reported window? The present result is undetermined; unresolved separation alone does not justify C (arXiv:2607.06621#r18, arXiv:2607.06621#r19). Would seed replication reproduce the head-level stage ordering in the 3M LM (arXiv:2402.02364#R1, arXiv:2402.02364#R5, arXiv:2402.02364#R7)? Would replicated 1-10B trajectories with matched component measures strengthen that scale beyond R0 (arXiv:2606.02378#r18, arXiv:2606.02378#r19, arXiv:2606.02378#r20)? Tests at 10B parameters or more would address the missing scale coverage (counts: versions.V7.studies_by_size). Confirming author independence would strengthen the R2 assignment.

sources.headline: A simplified transformer develops induction through ordered stages, learning what to output and attention keys.
Gradual learning of labels from context precedes and enables the abrupt induction transition.
Two induction heads form thousands of training steps apart through distinct transitions that partly overlap.
Induction heads form progressively from shallow to deep layers in a 162M Llama model.
Induction forms through successive stages: combining heads, tracking previous tokens, and matching preceding token sequences.
Induction-head learning has multiple plateaus, or periods of little change, in a high-dimensional toy model.
Markov-chain learning has multiple statistical stages, but rapidly switches to predicting tokens from the preceding token.
Causal clamps reveal three interacting subcircuits beneath a single observed phase change.
In a reasoning task, induction heads refine before a circuit that picks the final answer forms.
In-context n-gram learning jumps between plateaus of uniform guessing, bigram prediction, and trigram prediction.
Components for producing outputs, retrieving information, and tracking the previous token emerge in a fixed sequence.
Analysis separates how quickly model components learn to select information, copy it, and classify it.
Across checkpoints and model collections, previous-token heads emerge before the sharp change in induction and copying.
Decoders can use token associations before matching them to context in both training setups.
Heads tracking previous tokens precede heads matching preceding sequences and completed induction, through distinct developmental stages.
A two-layer synthetic model undergoes a second transition after induction first forms.
Induction heads join the eventual circuit at widely separated times, while some early heads fade.
Induction-head components emerge together after an earlier phase of learning to classify.
The minimal linear model largely skips the unigram learning stage.
Adding MLP layers leaves one intermediate plateau and combines positional learning within one head.
GPT2 recall accuracy slightly trails simultaneous changes in heads and internal representations, leaving formation sub-steps unresolved.
In Pythia, previous-token behavior appears before induction, but both emerge within the same sharp transition window.
A one-layer sequential model keeps improving gradually after induction forms, without a distinct second transition.
When recalling associations, patterns of copying and selecting information emerge together in a single phase transition.

untested.what: Measured overlap in time between sub-steps within one head's or one circuit's formation. Temporal overlap between different heads' transitions is also not quantified in arXiv:2410.02984; staggered development does not establish overlap.

wording_issues.issue: Internal sub-steps and staged strategy learning can coexist with an abrupt aggregate transition. In 2404.07129 the unclamped loss shows one phase change, while clamps identify interacting subcircuits; these experiments activate only Layer-2 Head 3, ablate the remaining Layer-2 heads, and clamp one Layer-1 head to perfect previous-token attention. In 2312.03002 a gradual preliminary phase precedes an abrupt transition where ILA1 and TILA2 appear together: separate emergence of those components is absent. In 2402.11004 the rapid bigram switch follows a long unigram plateau, with loss measured as test KL divergence. In Pythia-410m/160m, 2607.06621 reports previous-token behavior first, followed by induction behavior, the ICL proxy and wiring within 1–4B tokens; whether formation comprises separate transitions remains undetermined.

The order of sub-steps differs between settings. In 2306.00802's simplified two-layer trigger-output model, freezing experiments favor WO2, then WK2, then WK1 (first-layer previous-token). Easier WK2 learning is established by comparing freezing WK1 until iteration 300 with freezing WK2 until iteration 300; freezing WO2 separately establishes that output associations must be learned first. 2511.01033's verdict gives output, then retrieval, then previous-token. 2402.02364 finds the previous-token head before induction, with K-composition starting before attention-pattern changes. 2609.19000 resolves precursor-before-capability states; its cited previous-token score does not itself measure induction behavior. 'A sequence' therefore names no single order.

Overlap is almost never measured. Only 2410.02984's verdict calls its per-head transitions overlapping. Several studies list overlap as untested: lw:Zza9MNA7YtHkzAtit (LM3 and LM4 overlap not quantified), 2409.09281 (distinct versus overlapping not analysed) and 2609.32991 (overlap in loss or ICL not shown).

Metric lags and coarse sampling do not by themselves resolve formation sub-steps. In Pythia-410m/160m, 2607.06621 reports previous-token behavior first, followed by induction behavior, the ICL proxy and wiring within 1–4B tokens. Its explicit unresolved ordering concerns spectral structure versus function; separate formation transitions remain undetermined. In 2511.16893's GPT2 125M natural-data setting (batch 16, context 128), head-level scores and model-level recall metrics change roughly together, with associative-recall accuracy slightly later; no separate formation sub-steps are measured. In 2609.19000 the median valid-anchor time/emergence time ratio is 0.843. The trap-language anchor combines circuit and graded behavioral signals at the same evaluation, rather than measuring bare precursor formation alone. Halving the learning rate stretches the gap 2.27×.

method_sensitivity.factor: Architecture (attention-only versus MLP, transformer versus minimal model, layer count and recurrence)
method_sensitivity.what: Architecture changes the observed strategy plateaus and attention sub-steps. On a 3-gram task, attention-only transformers show prolonged plateaus and quick transitions; with MLP layers, one intermediate unigram plateau precedes a head acquiring (−1, −2)-token attention together (2508.12837). Second-layer induction behaviour is not measured. On Markov chains, a transformer goes uniform→unigram→bigram, with the induction-associated test-KL drop following a long unigram plateau (2402.11004). The minimal linear model largely skips that plateau; this alone does not establish fewer formation sub-steps. Its separate component-learning analysis supports sequential learning under specified curriculum conditions. A two-layer model shows a later second transition at 530M–620M tokens; one-layer sequential attention instead shows gradual refinement and a small ripple (lw:tiEgivi7crHSnSrH5). These results distinguish V7 staging from V2's full coincidence claim.

method_sensitivity.factor: Checkpoint resolution and how stages are detected
method_sensitivity.what: 2402.02364 states that stage boundaries depend on checkpoint spacing, smoothing, time versus log-time differentiation, and plateau tolerance. With 22 half-doubling checkpoints per model, 2607.06621 reports previous-token behaviour first in Pythia-410m/160m; induction behaviour, the ICL proxy and wiring follow within 1–4B tokens. The unresolved ordering concerns spectral structure versus function; separate formation transitions are neither established nor excluded. In 2606.02378, the first recall values for OLMo 1B (2B tokens) and OLMoE (20B tokens) are upper bounds set by the earliest published checkpoint. 2609.19000's leads (8→12B and 1→21B tokens) are bounded by the checkpoint grid.

method_sensitivity.factor: Imposed stage-splitting, freezing or layerwise training versus joint training; optimiser
method_sensitivity.what: 2409.10559 distinguishes imposed stage splitting from joint training. Theorem 3.6 concerns general TF(M,H,d,D), with H≥M and sufficiently large L; its finite validating simulation is separate. Joint training first favours the incorrect selector set {2,3}, followed by correct-selector dominance: observed V7 sub-phases, without measuring V2's compound transition. In 2306.00802, the easier-WK2-learning comparison freezes WK1 until iteration 300 versus freezing WK2 until iteration 300. Freezing WO2 separately establishes that output associations must be learned first. In 2410.11474, layerwise training separates the previous-token step by design. In its D=100 toy, GD and Adam differ: Adam escapes the plateau and shows several plateaus.

method_sensitivity.factor: Hyperparameters and data settings that move the gap between sub-steps
method_sensitivity.what: Halving the learning rate stretched the gap from precursor to induction 2.27× in two-layer fleets (2609.19000). In the minimal induction-head network with classifier, L=N=8 and B=1 remove the slow contextual-label phase: two of six seeds acquire ICL, while four converge slowly to a suboptimal minimum (2312.03002). This seed result concerns the minimal network. Class count and label count shift the timing of the phase change through different subcircuits (2404.07129, header). The speed and strategy staging of learning change with the transition-matrix distribution and with how useful unigram statistics are; the transition position varies across seeds (2402.11004, header). These strategy effects do not establish absence of separate formation sub-steps.

method_sensitivity.factor: Which signal is tracked (behaviour, attention score, LLC proxy, clamped loss)
method_sensitivity.what: In GPT2 125M, batch 16, context 128, natural data, prefix matching, logit attribution and associative-recall mean rank change abruptly around the same time; recall accuracy improves slightly later (2511.16893). This metric lag does not resolve V7 formation sub-steps. 2410.02984 uses data-refined LLC critical points, a complexity proxy. Developmental trajectories differ across evaluation datasets, but most stage boundaries persist; the authors attribute slight boundary shifts more likely to altered LLC-estimation hyperparameters than dataset differences. In 2404.07129, unclamped loss shows one phase change, while clamps expose interacting subcircuits. Section 4.2 activates only Layer-2 Head 3; fixing its attention to weight 1 on the correct label and 0 elsewhere isolates copy learning. This decomposition does not establish multiple separate transitions in unclamped training.
